content.overview: BNS s. 22 — Act of a person of unsound mind.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Unsoundness of mind: the person was incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that it was either wrong or contrary to law. The Standing Committee put “unsound mind” back in place of “mental illness”.
In student language: BNS s. 22 is the rule on “Act of a person of unsound mind”. The section provides that nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 22 exists so that “Act of a person of unsound mind” has a closed legal test in Chapter III — General Exceptions. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: When an act is not an offence: mistake, accident, infancy, unsoundness, consent, compulsion — and the right of private defence.

The provision in detail
22. Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law

Essential ingredients
1. Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 22 (Act of a person of unsound mind) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 22 (Act of a person of unsound mind), Chapter III — General Exceptions.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 22 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 22 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
